summary: Last Flight Log is an interactive web experience that introduces young learners to NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter through three defining moments: its first liftoff, its highest flight, and its final landing. Using NASA’s published flight log, visitors can compare how high Ingenuity flew and how long it stayed in the air on each flight. The story shows how a helicopter designed for up to five test flights went on to complete 72, proving powered, controlled flight was possible on another planet and helping Perseverance scout the terrain ahead.
details:
Project summary:

Last Flight Log is an interactive story for school-age space enthusiasts about Ingenuity, the first helicopter to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet. It follows three flights from the moment Ingenuity lifted off on Mars to the landing that ended its mission. The flight data let readers see what changed over the course of the mission.

How it works:

Select Flight 1, 61, or 72 to see its date, Martian day, maximum altitude, duration, and significance. Use the comparison controls to switch between altitude and duration. Bars use a common zero baseline and a fixed scale for each measurement. A downloadable CSV contains the three records shown in the interface.

The first flight was a 39.1-second test that reached 3 metres. Flight 61 reached 24 metres, the mission’s record. Flight 72 reached 12 metres and ended with rotor blade damage during landing. Perseverance later photographed the helicopter at its final airfield.

The project runs as a static website built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. It needs no account, installation, backend, or live data service. The original NASA photograph loads from NASA’s site when an internet connection is available. The flight story, controls, charts and CSV work offline.
dataRefs: Perseverance Spots Ingenuity at Its Final Airfield
